root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening, splitting, and separating something so that what is within or beyond it becomes exposed; it also has a distinct branch for something astonishing or overwhelming.
root_idea.development: The basic idea of cleaving extends to fissures, separated pieces, gaps between elevated things, the emergence of dawn, and the bringing forth of growth from grain and date-stones. A secondary lexical branch describes extraordinary things and great calamities.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form VII verb with an independently supported lexical meaning.
Quran-attested active participle with distinct divine-agent constructions.
Quran-attested noun with dawn and creation interpretations in the supplied evidence.

senses.definition: To split, cleave, or divide lengthwise; to become parted asunder.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, said of the sea becoming cleft apart.

senses.definition: One who splits or cleaves; specifically, the one who cleaves the grain and date-stones so that they produce green growth.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى in 6:95. The action may be understood as cleaving the covering to bring forth what grows within.

senses.definition: One who causes the dawn to break or appear.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ in 6:96, with dawn presented as emerging or spreading into view.

senses.definition: The creator or bringer-into-being of the grain, date-stones, or dawn.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported Quranic interpretation of the constructions in 6:95–96; this is an agentive interpretation distinct from the more concrete image of cleaving.

senses.definition: The dawn or daybreak; the light that breaks through and spreads.
senses.usage_conditions: The principal supplied lexical interpretation of الْفَلَقِ in 113:1. The Quran-focused discussion also records reported interpretations of this word as the rivers mentioned in 27:61 or as the utterance by which Moses was enabled to split the sea.

senses.definition: The whole of creation, or all created beings.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of الْفَلَقِ in 113:1, presenting creation as brought forth or made manifest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To split, cleave, or divide something lengthwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic transitive Form I verb; the intensive Form II is referred to the same lexical action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause the dawn or daybreak to break and appear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of God in the construction فَلَقَ الصُّبْحَ or فَلَقَ الْفَجْرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a palm tree, to split open so as to disclose the spathe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use describing the palm's opening growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To penetrate or travel far into the land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form I usage, compared in the source with غَلَقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The plucking of wool from a hide after it has become foul-smelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal-noun usage in the expression فَلَقَ صُوفَ الْجِلْدِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do or utter something remarkable or admirable; a مُفْلِق is a poet who composes remarkably.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a person's performance or poetry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity, misfortune, or exceptionally astonishing event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expressions may describe either a great misfortune or something so extraordinary that it provokes astonishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become skilled or proficient in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To crack or split in several places, or to become divided into fragments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an egg or similar object that has cracked extensively; the same derived form is also used of milk becoming separated or curdled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the dawn, to break or appear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive dawn construction; it is lexically distinct from the Quranic Form VII use for the sea only in its object and context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For milk, to become curdled, thickened, or separated into curds and whey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage describes milk becoming disunited through sourness or heat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run with such force or vehemence as to excite wonder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's remarkable exertion in running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a boy, to become large, bulky, and plump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized colloquial or rare Form Q.Q usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A split, fissure, cleft, or longitudinal division; also a cleft or ravine in a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can describe a fissure in a physical object, a mountain cleft, a gap in the mouth, or the line separating the hair at the middle of the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A half or split section of a rod or branch, especially wood split for making a bow; also a bow made from such split wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical object is defined by the prior splitting of its wood into two or more pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or open tract, gap, or passage between elevated areas such as hills, mountains, sand tracts, or camel humps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe a geographical depression or an intervening space between raised features.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hell, or a particular well within Hell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare noun usage attributed to specified authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The milk remaining at the bottom of a bowl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in an expression of reproach for a person associated with drinking such residue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden stock or restraint with holes that hold prisoners' legs in a row; also the thick staff used with a rope to secure a person's legs during flogging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun refers to a prisoner's restraint apparatus and related wooden implements.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ring-shaped brand beneath a camel's ear, marked by a perpendicular division.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized camel-marking term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece, fragment, or portion split off from something, including part of a bowl, bread, or a baked brick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may refer to one of divided halves or to a broken-off fragment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or she-goat with a broad or ample udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive expression for livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheer, unmixed lie.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The depressed or cleft part in the inner neck of a camel, around the passage of the windpipe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is specifically applied to the camel in the supplied evidence, not to a human anatomical feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vein, including a cephalic vein in the upper arm or a vein that swells in the neck; فَوَالِقُ are branching veins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collected quantity, or a small quantity, of hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records variation in the transmitted explanation between a collected and a small quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A broth or pottage into which fragments of bread are crumbled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional culinary term; one cited authority gives a different form for the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An army or military force, especially a great or formidable troop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is identified as the primary meaning of فَيْلَقٌ in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large, big, or imposing person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare personal epithet distinct from the military noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman characterized as cunning, evil, and clamorous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet in the expression فَيْلَقٌ applied to a woman or wife.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cocoon of the silkworm, from which silk is obtained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized technical word according to the cited lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exceptionally severe, violent, or far-reaching.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an especially harsh slaughter and of a journey remarkable for its extent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a peach, apricot, or similar fruit, splitting around its stone; in one vocalization, becoming dry as it splits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive participle for fruit whose flesh opens around the stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low, ignoble, poor, or propertyless man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also be applied figuratively to one lacking knowledge or understanding of a juridical ruling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who does or utters evil, disliked, or hateful things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate evaluative use of the same nominal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel bearing the فَلْقَة brand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participial designation for a branded camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The clear appearance of truth after it had been doubtful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing truth becoming manifest after uncertainty.

Fissure, cleft, ravine, and bodily cleft uses.
Low tract or gap between elevated areas.
Hell or a well in Hell.
Cleaving grain and date-stones; creator interpretation.
Causing dawn to break; creator interpretation.

cautions: The active participle فَالِق in 6:95–96 supports both concrete cleaving and reported creator-oriented interpretations; these are kept as separate senses.
